text:
james-support: forwarding a ticket from ACME Corp — they say they submitted a GDPR erasure request 36 hours ago and some tokens still resolve in their app. customer pasted logs and says deletion API returned 202 then later 200 but their downstream still sees embeddings. they asked for a timeline and proof-of-deletion bundle.

sara-support: copying the raw customer snippet: "DELETE /v1/customers/acme/records?scope=all => 202 Accepted, job_id=job_9f3a. Follow-up poll /jobs/job_9f3a returned status=completed. however embeddings.lookup('cust-123') still returns 1 vector."

maria-privsec: :eyes: can we confirm whether this tenant is hosted or Dedicated/private? that affects KMS/HSM key handling and subprocessor chain. also need to know if data residency pins to eu-west-1.

james-support: customer says Dedicated tenant in eu-west-1 (they have a committed instance id: ded-0452). they included the job_id above.

leo-sre: ok — likely causes: (1) eventual consistency between indexer and object store, (2) KV cache on serving nodes, or (3) KMS/HSM key rotation causing tombstone visibility delay. need these from customer: exact api request headers, job_id, the embedding id used in lookup, and a minimal repro curl.

anna-eng: can we get the backend audit logs for job_9f3a? I want the internal event stream showing delete -> tombstone -> purge. if key material was rotated we should see KMS ops in the same window.

james-support: asked customer for headers and embedding id, they gave embedding id = emb_acme_cust_123_v2 and a curl they ran: 

```
curl -X DELETE 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/customers/acme/records?scope=all' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"requester":"acme-ops","reason":"gdpr_erasure"}'
```

leo-sre: nice. ask them to run the read repro against a single node to avoid global cache: `REDWOOD_NODE=eu-node-03 curl http://eu-node-03.internal/embeddings/lookup?key=emb_acme_cust_123_v2` — that will tell us if it's per-node cache.

maria-privsec: for GDPR evidence we need an audit bundle: timestamps for request (client side), server ingress, KMS decrypt/encrypt logs, tombstone mark, and final purge. if customer requests DPA-level proof we must include subprocessor list for that region — listing KMS provider, object store, and any partner indexing service. I'll prepare the standard bundle template.

deploy-bot: Deploy successful: infra/kv-cache-flush job rolled out to eu-region at 1987654900 :white_check_mark:

leo-sre: good — we flushed KV caches at 1987654900. can someone check whether the customer observed change after that?

james-support: replied to customer — asked them to re-check and to run the node-specific lookup and to confirm after cache flush. also asked if they want the formal DPA bundle now or after we confirm purge.

sara-support: customer responded: after cache flush, lookup on eu-node-03 still returned vector. they said purge might not have executed; they want an export showing tombstone->purge timestamps and KMS key ops. requested ETA for formal evidence for compliance audit.

maria-privsec: escalate to privacy PMs + legal: we should aim to produce the DPA evidence package within 48 hrs if possible. meanwhile, we need the backend audit logs and KMS operation logs for job_9f3a and surrounding 24h.

anna-eng: I pulled the audit stream for job_9f3a: show entries at 1987654601 (ingress), 1987654630 (tombstone write), but I do not see a purge record — looks like purge worker skipped due to missing HSM key unwrap error at 1987654702. logging the HSM error id: hsm_err_7c1.

leo-sre: that matches: hsm_err_7c1 indicates our HSM failed to unwrap the per-tenant DEK for a short window during rotation — purge worker bails to avoid decrypting with the wrong key. fix is to requeue the purge once key unwrap succeeds.

james-support: communicated that to customer: told them purge delayed by transient HSM unwrap error, we requeued job_9f3a and will provide timestamps + HSM error id in bundle. asked if they need signed attestation or just logs.

sara-support: customer asked for signed attestation from KMS (they have legal checklist requiring evidence that key material was managed by an audited HSM).

maria-privsec: note — for Dedicated customers we include HSM access logs and KMS provider attestation when requested. legal will coordinate. I'll start a secure share prep.

anna-eng: requeue completed at 1987654988, purge executed at 1987655009, final tombstone removed from index at 1987655018. HSM unwrap succeeded at 1987654987 (hsm_event_322).

james-support: relayed final timestamps to customer and attached preliminary audit bundle (redwood internal logs + HSM event ids). customer confirmed vectors no longer returned from node checks. they requested the full subprocessor list for eu-west-1 and a copy of our DPA (they said their legal team needs the signed attestation).

maria-privsec: I'll attach subprocessor list (eu-west-1): Redwood KMS provider: CloudHSM Ltd (HSM with FIPS 140-2), Object store: EU-ObjectStore Inc., Indexer partner: FastIndex BV. also attach our DPA excerpt for erasure obligations and attestation process.

leo-sre: action items: (1) include HSM event ids and logs in bundle, (2) add note about requeue reason (unwrap error), (3) confirm purge timestamp, (4) verify no residual cache on other nodes.

james-support: closing loop with customer, uploading final signed bundle to s3 share and sending secure link. marking internal incident for TTL traceability.

sara-support: customer replied :thumbsup: and said legal accepted the evidence. closing ticket.

maria-privsec: filing a short post-incident note for the privacy playbook: consider adding automatic requeue telemetry and an alert when HSM unwraps occur during purges.

anna-eng: filing internal PR to improve retry logic for purge worker.

james-support: thanks all — good cross-team response.
